title: Defending Humanity at the Root: A Different Radicalism
author: Kim C. Domenico
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/Screenshot-2026-07-23-at-7.09.04-PM-680x459.png)

Photo by [Zach
Reiner](https://unsplash.com/@_zachreiner_?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

> “If you knock out the pillars of a sacred order, at the primal level such a
> change is experienced by people as a deep and lasting trauma, whether they
> know it or not.”  ____
>
> –Paul Kingsnorth,  _Against the Machine: the Unmaking of Humanity_ ____
>
> In Freud's own vision, the psyche wasn't built for bliss but for something
> more equivocal—ordinary unhappiness [as opposed to neurotic misery]  ____
>
> –Anna Ballan,  _Freud in the Age of Therapy-Speak_ , The Hedgehog Review
> ____
>
> Neurosis and creation… spring from the same soil ____
>
> – _Ibid._____
>
> “Things come to the poor that can't get to the door of the rich… It is a
> great privilege to be poor,—one that no man ever coveted, and but a very few
> have sought to retain, but yet one that many have learned to prize. You must
> not…. imagine it as a virtue; it is but a privilege, and one that, like
> other privileges, may be terribly misused.” ____
>
> –George MacDonald,  _The Princess and Curdie_ (1883), a children's fantasy
> novel ____

__Defending humanity? A grand-sounding idea, but how, actually, do we get
behind it? Do we think about all those people deserving compassion - the
indigenous, the victims of racist oppression, the colonized, LGBTQ people? Is
it them we can strenuously, passionately defend? But something is missing in
this picture. What about our white, liberal, resource-consuming, giant carbon
footprint, globe-trotting selfie-taking selves? We who inherited the wonders-
filled empire built upon the backs of enslaved people on land ripped off from
Native people, left to us by the Dead White Men we hate?  ____

Defending humanity without including myself in it? –  _what does that even
mean?_ Is it too egoistical of white, liberal, secular, top-of-the-heap me to
include  _myself_ in humanity that's worth saving? Too “undemocratic?” This
question, to me, gets to the heart of the liberal quagmire, to its
fecklessness. The only conscious concept we (I include myself) can have of the
good, it seems, is good for others. We do not see that leaving oneself  _out_
of what must be defended is the biggest ego trip of all! We cannot see where
polite modesty, tolerance, and putting oppressed others first has gotten us.
It's all phony baloney. It is based  _not_ in genuine respect and esteem for
the other, but in personal worthlessness, in servile egos that have adapted to
worshipping the reality we're given without any effort whatsoever on our part,
as if it were God. And this, all in the name of not serving any God, or any
master!  ____

+++____

The invitation to speak at the Utica Unitarian-Universalist church I received
a few months ago requested I speak as a “radical business owner.” While I
would not have called our coffeeshop that existed in Utica for 22 years
_radical_ , still the use of that term made me feel seen, not all that usual
in my post-Cafe Domenico life in Utica, so, a little grateful, I accepted. And
I got thinking about radicalism, and why it wasn't quite the right word to
describe our business or its offshoot, The Other Side arts space.____

Radicalism in politics is generally understood to mean going to  _the root_
(from Latin “ _radix_ ,”) of the social economic problem – i.e., capitalism -
and thus calling for extreme, or revolutionary change against slower,
reformist kinds of change. The problem with radicalism, even for those of us
who agree capitalism is the problem, is very few people – that illustrious
roster of heroes who've stood for truth and the common good, often martyrs,
excepted - are inclined to take up radical activism. This was so even before
these days of militarized police and jailings – not to mention shootings - of
peaceful protesters. Many of us want a normal, family-centered life in the old
way, familiar routines, being useful in some way, not a life on the lam from
the F.B.I.____

__Not to take anything away from the heroism of activist heroes, or, on the
other hand, to say that numbers are important. We can of course blame the
attainment of bourgeois well-being for the widespread passivity on the left in
the face of increasing and alarming threats to humanity and our earthly home;
there is truth to this, hunger being spur to rebellion. Or, we can see that
traditional radical activism, though it takes seriously the evil of
capitalism, may be looking at the wrong “root.” Perhaps, instead of the roots
of the _problem_ we should be concerned with the roots of our shared humanity
in  _cultures,_ cultures __ that are, and have always been “tied down by, and
to, things solid, timeless and…lasting” (Kingsnorth), i.e., rooted! Maybe we
are experiencing a different starvation, that of our souls, starved of
cultural nourishment. If we were to feel  _that_ hunger, would we be on to
something hearts could feel passion for, and would passionately defend?____

For a very long time, influenced by imaginative thinkers like archetypal
psychologist Carl G. Jung and mythologist Joseph Campbell, and most crucially,
due to my own experience, I have taken it seriously that heroism is a
universal call. Its call is not exclusively to some “geniuses,” but issues
from the soul in every man and woman. The 'call,' I judge, is not  _first_ to
challenge capitalism or rightwing extremists on the streets or in Congress, or
even to redistribute the wealth, though I am as excited as anyone by what
Mayor Mamdani is doing in NYC (i.e., with free childcare, etc.).  ________

For liberals, we who benefit most from the economy as it is, and whose
political stands of the moment are tempered by our privilege, the radical call
is different. It is to regain the ground from which _humanity can be defended_
by __ taking up the very personal struggle to achieve the fullness of one's
singular humanity. This very different, sort of “monastic” activism can only
build, with patience and temerity and faith, from the ground up and will, by
its nature, change what “activism” is. The process of dehumanization did not
begin with the invention of the Internet. But the looming threat of human
replacement by machine now seems a culmination, in the West, of our _not_
acting to defend humanity, of ordinary peoples' constant giving way to the
mesmerizing siren song of progress. It was only a matter of time before those
in whom we have entrusted our salvation, the techno-wizards – would provide a
solution for the problems that have perpetually dogged humanity, keeping us
predictably imperfect, error-prone, capable of horrific brutality.  ____

It's now or never if we will make the determination if humanity is worth
saving. The crisis is real. It presents an opportunity for those of us who do
not – for whatever reason - participate in radical activism. That is, for me,
and others like me, radical activism will only be generated at “the root of my
being.” It has to be in defense of something personally real _for me. It has
to be_ that thing that is something I would die for. Like many mothers, I can
say rather automatically I would sacrifice my life for my children, an animal
level instinct. But what about at the level of that which distinguishes me as
a human being? I have found there is one thing alone I can say I would die
for; that is  _the truth of knowing I am_ loved _in my humanity_.____

For sure, in this matter of the heart I speak of a transcendent, metaphysical
truth, completely unverifiable, esoteric, perhaps evidence of my weakness,
unquestionably a sign of my vulnerability. As a basis for moral judgment this
_knowing one is loved_ is __ related to,_but not the same as_ , the truth
popular in the liberal world that we are “part of the interdependent web.”
Other than virtually, via Internet, the latter, euphonious truth is mostly not
lived out. That is, if it were, if we lived with our awareness constantly on
the common good, our nation would not be sucking up the vast majority of the
world's resources, contributing the most to global warming; we would not be
living alienated and lonely lives (in)secure in the arms of bourgeois reality.
_If it were lived out, people would choose limitations_ , we would bring our
way of life down to the sustainable, to “poverty,” to some form of “in-
commonness.” Bourgeois attainments – TV and shopping and travel! - would no
longer be the ultimate comfort. How radical is that?____

+++____

This “roots radicalism” could conceivably catch on, be a viable a movement on
the secular left (though a paradoxical one, moving backward instead of
forward, conservatively). It regains the passion, but not the dangerous mob
appeal of a call to MAGA, or its related blood-and-soil Aryan nostalgia
looking to a fuehrer to save 'the people.' A back-to-the-roots movement could
happen, that is, if liberals can get out of their own way and allow in
themselves the  _depth move_ toward reclaiming and restoring their human
roots. That movement is, partly, the kind of settling, and self-limitation in
commitment to place and relationships over time made famous by Wendell Berry.
It is, certainly, a relearning of human skills of cultivating, building and
maintaining, a kind of voluntary poverty that is  _not_ simply “anti-
progress.” It is not about women going back to enslavement in biological
necessity! Or about being anti-science. But it must reach from the level of
_doing_ , where so much of what we “know” is second hand, a matter of
agreement within our preferred social milieu, into the level of being, to the
need of the very soul to feel safe and protected, that will, in its turn,
gives one one's own knowing.____

__' Roots radicalism' depends upon restoration of imagination's place in
consciousness for proper orientation in this life, a place it had throughout
most of human history. In the world that's had its sacred order knocked out,
the bottomline feeling of unsafety will never be met socially, even among
people working for shared purpose. It comes, fundamentally, in personal
relationship with the Unconscious – i.e., with one's own darkness, the
spiritual _crisis_ that gives imagination its humanity-supportive role. Herein
lie the (sacred, metaphysical) roots of culture - a relationship with depth -
and height- that can come with acknowledging the authority of that imaginative
voice in the soul. Freud's work opened that perilous descent (_katabasis_)
into depth by means of the psychotherapeutic encounter. It made “ordinary
unhappiness” possible (though not easy!) by continuous mental effort. One
could live with less – with “poverty. ” That is, “things come to the poor that
do not come to the door of the rich.__

However, denial is so powerful, and so largely tacitly supported,
transformational psychotherapy is rarely taken up except when an individual's
pain makes them desperate (and they have the money, or the insurance coverage,
to pay for it). Thus most people remain ignorant of knowing that the way
opened via one's pain fits the term “redemptive.”  ________

In fact, many of us have no way of knowing our pain is authentically pain! Not
even dignifiable as suffering! It's too easy to think of one's pain as  _“ I
'm just depressed while everyone else seems happier.”_ When acute, it can be
treated with pharmaceuticals. As well, the  _semblance_ of psycho-spiritual
knowledge can be had by more convenient means, such as self-diagnosis, and the
essentially shallow world of online wisdom-sharing and influencing. Apparently
even the psychotherapeutic profession that owes its existence to Freud, avoids
use of talk therapy (in 2005, only 11% of therapists used it in their
practice, according to Bruce Levine, in Counterpunch 7/10/26)!____

+++____

Our Cafe was a this-world embodiment of “roots radicalism,” a realization of
the sacrality of place. Since its loss I struggle to regain my inward balance.
For 22 years, I took its protective space for granted. Assaulted by constant
news of bombing, wars, immigrant arrests, and with a share of domestic
troubles, not to mention hazardous air quality caused by Canadian wildfires,
I'm back struggling with the sorting out of powerful feelings  _that
originated in trauma_ and are  _still there in my wounded soul_. Only
gradually, with great difficulty, since I partake of few of the distractions
that keep so many people going in the “machine-syntonic” way, am I able to
block the neurotic attribution of blame to myself, or, perhaps worse, nurse
resentments. And to be clear, resentments against Trump are no less neurotic
than any other kind!____

I divulge personal information only to show this embarrassing, unworthy
struggle with “the neurotic repetition” has valid basis in the experience of
trauma. And, equally, it is preoccupation with self. It supports neither
positive egoic projects, a la Mamdani, nor the alive soul. For us traumatized
people, neuroses are the essence of being unfree, “the endless repetition of
the mistake that mankind at large has chosen to sanctify.” (D.H. Lawrence). To
be simply able to “love and work” in Freud's famous formula, is  _not_ a
simple matter! It is heroic challenge. And it has great moral consequence for
one's existence in liberal reality. Where denial of trauma is common, but the
depth work that brings one back to “the soil of creation” is rare, we exist in
a desolate, frightening, atomized horizontal context fit for machines, not for
human beings. No wonder we are averse to opening that door to personal trauma!
But with trauma left buried in the unconscious, the ego is free to make its
preferred distinctions, at worst easily yielding to prejudice and hatred, at
“best,” serving the liberal good that's not good enough to build our lives in
defiance of the Machine.____

At this “senior” point in my life, to experience the saving awareness of being
seen and loved “in the perspective of Eternity” demands of me now mostly that
I use my “God-like” creativity consciously. That is, despite the 10 million
misgivings my ego assaults me with, despite the urgency of the global moment
and the multiple threats to human beings and the earth calling for radical
response, the demand of the soul is that I practice an art that is my own,
that I connect subversively in this way with the truth of my real freedom. It
does not change my personal reality, that is confining beyond what I bargained
for. But in allowing me to remember, in the act of creating, the discovery of
my alive soul – I am provided with a reality unshakably counter to that of
confinement; the equal truth that I am free, the wisdom in“ordinary
unhappiness” can be attained.
